I can't tell from the first video (the camera bleaches out the hologram), but I will take his word for it. In his second video the hologram turns yellow at one angle. Is this normal for a narrow band reflection hologram? I would have thought the image to just disappear if the hologram was narrow band at the extreem angles. How can it be replaying yellow if it is truely narrow band. Maybe it is I who is missing something. Or again, maybe it is the camera.

excellent questions john, because dcg reflection holograms change color when being replayed in white light, so how to test If a hologram is narrowband and what happen to the efficiency as it become more broad band?

i would like to put this to the test............

My thoughts here;

 The replay angle should remain constant or static, change the replay angle (in white light) and change wavelength selectivity of the hologram .

Possibly a way to record how efficient theye are ,is to replay of both WL and NB holograms in collimated white light source and view the green replay (using a CD or prism )of both holograms ………….

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
I use one of these spectrometers for casual measuring of bandwidths: [http://www.starlab.com/psprod.html#Anchor-Plastic-23240](http://www.starlab.com/psprod.html#Anchor-Plastic-23240)

It's very accurate and easily readable to 1nm! Highly recommended for every holographer.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: I guess I should have mentioned that I use the plastic version. A great deal for $25! The cardboard version is probably as good if build up well.
